var slot: Int32 = 4
withUnsafeMutablePointer(to: &slot) { port in
    port.pointee = 9
}
return slot

F04.P2.justification: ArraySlice (xs[1...3] or a slicing view) shares storage with the original Array via copy-on-write without an eager copy; window[0]... reads without copying.

F04.P3.justification: === is Swift's standard reference-identity operator for class instances, distinct from ==.

F05.P1.justification: f(x) — ordinary bare call syntax; Array has value semantics (COW) so no sigil is required or available at the call site.

F05.P2.justification: func put(_ cell: inout Int32) { cell = 12 }; put(&cell) — inout is Swift's dedicated explicit writable-parameter-passing form.

F05.P3.justification: let neg: (Int32) -> Int32 = { a in k - a }; let ys = xs.map(neg) — closures are first-class values capturing k, referenced by name at the map call site.

F09.P2.justification: xs.sorted(by: >) explicitly supplies the descending comparator (a new array is produced, not an in-place reorder); let lt = a < b.

F11.P2.justification: let part = xs[1..<4]; return part[1] — ArraySlice shares storage with xs (documented COW sharing) rather than eagerly copying.

F12.P1.fragment:

let n = o ?? 0

F13.P2.justification: do { n = try parse(s) } catch { n = 0 } — do/catch is Swift's normal local-handling construct with a visible protected region.

F14.P1.justification: enum Shape { case circle(r: Double); case rect(w: Double, h: Double) } — enum is a closed, exhaustively-checked sum type; language rules forbid adding a case from elsewhere.

F14.P2.justification: switch s { case .circle(let r): ...; case .rect(let w, let h): ... } with no default — the Swift compiler statically requires exhaustive coverage of enum cases.

F14.P3.justification: protocol Shape { func area() -> Double }; struct Circle/Rect in unit shapes, struct Tri: Shape in a separate unit dispatched through the Shape existential — protocol-based extensibility across units, scored under the frozen multi-unit recipe (toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes).

F15.P1.justification: func head<T>(_ xs: [T]) -> T { xs[0] } reused at Int32 and String — Swift generics preserve the T -> T static relationship (no type erasure to Any).

F15.P2.justification: func max_of<T: Comparable>(_ a: T, _ b: T) -> T { a > b ? a : b } — Comparable constraint is stated at the generic declaration and checked there.

F15.P3.justification: protocol Named { func tag() -> String }; let items: [Named] = [A(), B()]; items[0].tag() — existential array dispatches to the concrete implementation at runtime without static knowledge of the concrete type.

F16.P1.justification: let xs = [1, 2, 3]; let total = xs.reduce(0, +) — reduce is the standard-library summation form (fewer tokens than a manual for-loop).

F16.P2.fragment:

let total = mp.values.reduce(0, +)
let miss = mp["b"] ?? 0

F17.P1.justification: func read_all() throws -> Int { let fh = try FileHandle(forReadingFrom: url); defer { fh.closeFile() }; let text = ...; return text.count } — defer runs on every exit path including the throwing path, and the release point is visible at the defer statement.

F17.P2.justification: class Handle { let id: Int32; deinit { released += 1 } } — deinit is Swift's documented end-of-lifetime hook, run deterministically when ARC drops the last strong reference in the non-cyclic case exercised here.

F18.P1.justification: print("x") — Swift.print is available without any import in a normal Swift program; no declaration is required.

F18.P2.justification: module util { public func pub_add(...) { ... secret() }; private func secret() -> Int32 { 1 } }; external call util.pub_add(2,3) — access control (public/private) and module boundaries are enforced by the compiler, scored under the frozen multi-unit recipe.

F19.P1.fragment:
async let x = 20
async let y = 22
let sum = await x + y
return sum

F19.P2.justification: actor Counter { var count: Int64 = 0; func inc() { count += 1 } } incremented 1000 times each from two Tasks awaiting inc() — actor isolation is documented by Swift to serialize access and eliminate data races on the actor's state.

F20.P1.justification: import Glibc/Darwin; let r = abs(Int32(-3)) — Swift's built-in C-interop module exposes libc functions directly with no third-party binding generator.

F20.P2.fragment:
@_cdecl("add2")
public func add2(_ a: Int32, _ b: Int32) -> Int32 { return a + b }
F20.P2.justification: @_cdecl("add2") func add2(_ a: Int32, _ b: Int32) -> Int32 { a + b } is the only mechanism Swift ships for a stable unmangled C-ABI export, but @_cdecl is an underscored, documented-as-unstable/internal compiler attribute rather than a fully public, non-experimental API.
